D017_m001.question:
Well… it really started getting bad about two, maybe three years ago. I live out on the station most of the year, so I’ve got a lot of time alone, and I end up in front of the mirror in the washroom more than I should. It’s mainly my face and upper body. My teeth look all wrong to me—crooked, yellow, too big. My chest looks deformed, like one side sinks in more, and I can’t stop staring at it. And my hairline… every day I’m convinced it’s creeping back further.

When I do get into town for supplies, I can’t focus on anything because I’m sizing up every man I see—his jawline, his teeth, his build—always deciding I look misshapen in comparison. Same with people on TV or in magazines; I’ll fixate on their straight teeth or full hair and then come back to the station feeling sick looking at myself.

It’s gotten to the point where I’ve delayed maintenance runs because I’m stuck re-checking the mirror or changing shirts. I avoid the pub and even video calls with the coast office because I’m sure everyone’s staring at how wrong I look.

A. Body Dysmorphic Disorder
    B. Bipolar I Disorder with Psychotic Features
    C. Persistent Depressive Disorder
    D. Major Depressive Disorder

D017_m002.question:

It’s gotten to the point that I avoid social events and even turn down some work because I don’t want people seeing me. I’m constantly late to fittings because I change clothes over and over, trying to hide my body.
